messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - Increased 5xx from serving-runtime on region-us-west1. Symptom: repeated cudaErrorIllegalAddress / SIGSEGV in model-worker containers. Affected nodes: gpu-relay-23, gpu-relay-27, gpu-relay-31. Triggering stack: kernel pagewalk -> driver -> container.

oncall: I'm on it, paging @maya (SRE) to triage.

maya (SRE): taking lead. I see correlated OOMs then illegal address faults in the same timeframe. Starting repro logs capture and will cordon nodes.

sasha (eng-runtime): noted. Recent rollout of v2.14 runtime had a memory-mapping tweak for KV cache prefetching — could be related. I will pull the crash logs and heap traces now.

kevin (infra): nodes cordoned: gpu-relay-23 and gpu-relay-31. Drain in progress on gpu-relay-27 (low traffic). No mass reboots yet.

maya (SRE): attaching container stderr from gpu-relay-23 (excerpts):
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] worker[pid=4123] CUDA error: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered
stack: 0x7f8e6f.. <runtime_kernel.cu:213>
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] container: killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
```

sasha (eng-runtime): and kernel dmesg from same host shows pagewalk invalid address:
```
Mar 15 14:02:12 gpu-relay-23 kernel: iommu: device 0000:85:00.0: invalid device address 0x7f5b2000, fault reason: misaligned address
Mar 15 14:02:12 gpu-relay-23 kernel: BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref in pagewalk+0x1a2/0x3c0
```

maya (SRE): pattern: svc spikes -> kernel misaligned pagewalk -> containers crash with illegal address. Could be a kernel/driver race under high pagewalk concurrency.

oncall: evidence of customer-impact?

tara (support): yes, support tickets show elevated errors for customers using streaming chat endpoints in us-west1 since ~14:00. Affected customers: cust-zenith, cust-aurora (high). I started templated incident message to affected accounts.

dan (customer-success): I can escalate contract teams. Need ETA for mitigation before I message legal/comms.

maya (SRE): immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale routing away from us-west1 by adjusting smart-routing policy to prefer us-east1 for GPUs, 2) disable v2.14 runtime rollout (rollback to v2.13) in affected pool, 3) cordon + reboot suspicious nodes after collecting & uploading full crash dumps to /tmp/incidents/5412345678, 4) enable CPU-fallback routing for low-latency-but-lower-throughput customers if needed.

sasha (eng-runtime): rolling back runtime on dedicated pool now (canary first). If that removes the prefetch path, we should see reduced pagewalk concurrency.

kevin (infra): starting node reboots on gpu-relay-23 after dump. Will monitor NV driver logs.

maya (SRE): setting oncall escalation: if more illegal address faults appear after rollback and reboots, escalate to kernel team and consider immediate node evacuation and customer failover.

sasha (eng-runtime): quick repro attempt: ran load test against v2.14 on a dev node with synthetic prefix reuse pattern. After ~2000 concurrent requests saw early illegal address in GPU driver. Log snippet: `E [driver] illegal device addr 0x7f9a4000 in memcpy_async`. Will collect a minimized repro.

oncall: OK. Priorities: (P1) stop customer impact, (P2) collect forensic, (P3) find root cause.

maya (SRE): update for customers: initial mitigation (routing + rollback) applied at 14:18. Error rate dropped ~55% across the pool but still seeing sporadic faults during drain.

tara (support): copy. Sending update to cust-zenith and cust-aurora: "We're routing traffic away from impacted nodes and rolling back a recent runtime change. We're monitoring and will update in 30 mins."

sasha (eng-runtime): can confirm canary rollback to v2.13 removed the prefetch path. Canary instance passed sustained load for 45m with no illegal address hits. Preparing a hotfix branch with extra bounds-checking in the prefetch path to test post-incident.

kevin (infra): gpu-relay-23 back online after reboot, kernel logs clean so far. Keeping it cordoned until full repro artifacts uploaded.

maya (SRE): collecting crash dumps and kernel oops into the incident bucket. Filing ticket for kernel/driver root-cause triage: possible iommu misalignment/race.

sasha (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) ship hotfix with conservative mapping (disable speculative prefetch) and extra logging to detect misaligned address attempts, 2) run broader canary across 3 nodes in us-east1, 3) coordinate with kernel team if repro is reliable.

oncall: estimated time to partial resolution (routing + rollback): 45m. Full resolution: dependent on kernel triage, unknown.

maya (SRE): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~0.9% of global requests experienced 500s during the spike window; highest impact in us-west1 streaming chat. No data loss reported. Affected nodes were mitigated via routing and rollback.

tara (support): ticket updates posted. Customers acknowledged and are monitoring. Some asked for root-cause - I'll tell them we'll share postmortem once kernel/driver analysis completes.

dan (customer-success): prepping customer-facing timeline and SLAs impact assessment.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied: routing override and runtime rollback at 14:18. Monitor will recheck for 1h.

maya (SRE): leaving follow-up tasks: collect full kernel traces, run the minimized repro from sasha under instrumentation, prepare postmortem draft, and schedule kernel meeting with vendor if repro matches driver bug.

sasha (eng-runtime): noting root-cause candidates: 1) speculative KV prefetch in v2.14 triggers misaligned device-address walks under concurrent eviction; 2) GPU driver mishandles misaligned scatter/gather; 3) kernel iommu bug. Need stackwalk + address translation mapping to narrow.

kevin (infra): I'll coordinate with cloud provider support for any hypervisor/iommu updates and check for recent host kernel patches that may have regressed.

maya (SRE): thanks all. Leaving channel open for updates. If anyone sees new illegal address faults, ping here and escalate.

oncall: good job team. :thumbsup:
